headline: International Holding Company converts warrants into equity in Sammaan Capital
hook: IHC raises stake to over thirty percent
summary: International Holding Company (IHC) has converted 8.69 crore warrants into equity shares in Sammaan Capital, increasing its shareholding from 28.34% to 33.32%. This conversion represents a major capital infusion from a prominent investor into the housing finance company. Indian retail investors should note this significant shift in promoter and major shareholder dynamics, which alters the ownership structure of the firm.
why_it_matters: Major stakeholder increases commitment to Sammaan Capital
winners_losers: Sammaan Capital gains / diluted shareholders hurt

headline: Sammaan Capital makes timely interest payment on secured NCDs
hook: Timely debt servicing by Sammaan Capital
summary: Sammaan Capital Limited has certified that it made timely payment of interest on its Secured Redeemable Non-Convertible Debentures issued via public issue. The disclosure was made pursuant to Regulation 57 of SEBI Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements Regulations, 2015. Such routine debt servicing filings confirm meeting of financial obligations on listed NCDs. Retail bondholders receive their scheduled payouts as mandated.
why_it_matters: Bondholders receive scheduled interest payouts on time.

headline: Sammaan Capital allots over 8.68 crore equity shares to promoter Avenir Investment RSC
hook: Promoter stake rises via warrant conversion
summary: Sammaan Capital Limited has allotted 8,68,92,966 fully paid-up equity shares to its promoter, Avenir Investment RSC Ltd. The allotment is executed through the conversion of previously issued warrants. This corporate action changes the company's equity capital structure and promoter shareholding. Retail investors should track equity dilution and promoter confidence signals from this capital adjustment.
whats_next: Listing and trading approval for the newly allotted shares on exchanges
why_it_matters: Promoter shareholding changes affect equity dilution and voting power.

headline: Sammaan Capital Q2 disbursements grow 55% QoQ
summary: Sammaan Capital reported a nearly 55% quarter-on-quarter increase in disbursements for the September quarter. Following the announcement, the stock jumped 5% in intraday trade. Brokerage firm Ventura Securities maintains a 'Buy' rating on the stock with a target price of Rs 377.70 per share. Retail investors can view this as a sign of business momentum recovery, directly impacting the stock's near-term price action.
why_it_matters: Disbursal growth signals improving credit momentum for the company.
winners_losers: Sammaan Capital shareholders gain / none hurt

headline: Sammaan Capital reports Q2 FY27 disbursements of Rs 6,000 crore and AUM exceeding Rs 59,000 crore
hook: Disbursements jump 55 percent at Sammaan Capital
summary: Sammaan Capital announced provisional Q2 FY27 disbursements of approximately Rs 6,000 crore, up from Rs 3,875 crore in Q1 FY27. Assets Under Management grew to over Rs 59,000 crore as of September 30, 2026, compared to Rs 56,239 crore at the end of June. The company added over 30,700 new customers during the quarter and expanded its branch network to 245. This data is provisional and subject to statutory audit review.
whats_next: Audited financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026
why_it_matters: Stronger loan growth signals improving momentum for Sammaan Capital
